questions.q: According to the lecture, what is the **first** step in the technology of preparing methodological developments?
options: Choosing GIS software for the route
Defining the learning objectives and expected outcomes
questions.explain: Topic 8: the technology begins with defining learning objectives and expected outcomes, which depend on the audience.

questions.q: Which elements belong to a **scripted excursion program** (Topic 8)?
options: Stages: introduction, main stops, transitions, conclusion
Key talking points and visual aids
questions.explain: Topic 8: the script includes stages, timing, key talking points, aids and interactive parts. Hidden commissions are an ethics violation (Topic 12).

questions.q: Which international organization recommends best practices for tour design, visitor engagement and ethical storytelling?
questions.explain: Topic 8: the World Federation of Tourist Guide Associations (WFTGA) recommends these best practices.

questions.q: Which discipline helps the guide decode styles, symbolic motifs and aesthetic principles, e.g. Renaissance vs. Romanticism in the Louvre?
questions.explain: Topic 9: architecture and art history let the guide decode styles and symbols, as in the Louvre example.

questions.q: Robben Island excursions in South Africa are a case study of interdisciplinary guiding because they are led by…
questions.explain: Topic 9: former political prisoners combine first-hand testimony with historical and political interpretation.

questions.q: According to the lecture, children usually respond better to storytelling, visual cues and gamification, while adults often prefer structured explanations and discussion.
questions.explain: Topic 9: this is the contribution of pedagogy to excursions.

questions.q: The technique of narrative construction (interpretive guiding) is rooted in the heritage interpretation principles of…
questions.explain: Topic 10: interpretive guiding comes from Freeman Tilden's principles of heritage interpretation.

options: The guide, the object and the group form a triangle for good visibility and audibility
A route with three main stops
A triangle of questions: who, what, why
questions.explain: Topic 10: the position-triangle is a site-positioning technique for visibility, audibility and safety.

questions.q: Which are **interactive techniques** named in Topic 10?
questions.explain: Topic 10: interactive techniques include Q&A, quizzes, role-play, dramatization and simulation games.

questions.q: Which type of excursion usually follows a linear structure: introduction – observation of the process – Q&A – conclusion?
questions.explain: Topic 11: industrial and technical excursions (e.g. a brewery in Germany) follow this linear structure.

questions.q: In dark tourism excursions, such as Auschwitz-Birkenau, the guide should use sensational stories to keep the group entertained.
questions.explain: Topic 11: the guide must avoid sensationalism and create a space for reflection, using testimonies, archives and verified statistics.

questions.q: Which audience typically wants **brevity, entertainment and photo opportunities**?
questions.explain: Topic 11: mass tourists prefer brevity, entertainment and photos; academic groups want analysis and discussion.

questions.q: In an excursion institution, the collection of research, maps and visual aids for a new tour that guides use in training is called…
questions.explain: Topic 12: methodologists compile materials in a methodological dossier used as a reference during training.

questions.q: Which are functions of the **methodological work of an excursion institution** (Topic 12)?
options: Monitoring and evaluation of guide performance
Selling hidden commissions to souvenir shops
questions.explain: Topic 12: methodological work includes scenarios, training, monitoring, innovation and market research. Hidden commissions break professional ethics.

questions.q: Which centralized Soviet organization promoted excursion tourism for citizens and international visitors?
questions.explain: Topic 13: Intourist and the All-Union Society for Cultural Relations promoted ideologically framed excursions in the USSR.

questions.q: In Belarus, excursion tourism largely revolves around the memory of World War II, with sites such as the Brest Fortress and the Khatyn Memorial.
questions.explain: Topic 13: Belarus focuses on WWII memory, Orthodox traditions and Soviet-era industrial heritage.

questions.q: Which national project lists sacred sites used for religious and pilgrimage excursions in Kazakhstan, e.g. Beket-Ata and Aisha-Bibi?
questions.explain: Topic 14: the national project "Sacred Geography of Kazakhstan" includes the Turkestan mausoleums, Beket-Ata and Aisha-Bibi.

questions.q: Which is **not** one of the four challenges of excursion tourism in Kazakhstan named in Topic 14?
options: Shortage of trained and certified guides
Too many international tourists in every region
questions.explain: Topic 14: the challenges are guides, infrastructure, marketing/digital presence and the legal framework.
